findings.title: Cron still schedules emails for reminders marked cancelled
findings.body: The `unscheduledReminders` query filters only on `method: EMAIL`, `scheduled: false` and `scheduledDate <= now+72h`, but not on `cancelled`. Reminders for bookings that were cancelled/rescheduled before they were ever handed to SendGrid (i.e. created with `scheduled: false`, `referenceId: null`, then flagged `cancelled: true` by `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`) will therefore be picked up here, sent to SendGrid with a future `sendAt`, and the reminder email will be delivered for a cancelled booking — exactly the bug this PR aims to fix. Add `cancelled: { not: true }` (or delete such rows at cancel time when `referenceId` is null).

findings.title: Cancellation loop aborts on first failure and does not filter method/referenceId
findings.body: `remindersToCancel` is not filtered by `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` nor by `referenceId != null`. A row with `referenceId: null` (never scheduled) or an SMS row will produce a SendGrid POST with `batch_id: null`/a Twilio SID, which throws. Because the whole `for` loop is inside a single `try`, one such failure aborts cancellation of every remaining reminder in the batch, so other scheduled emails for cancelled bookings are still sent. Filter the query and wrap each request in its own try/catch.

findings.title: immediateDelete path leaves orphan WorkflowReminder rows
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true the SendGrid send is cancelled and the function returns early without deleting (or flagging) the `workflowReminder` row. Callers using this path (handleNewBooking reschedule, workflow/step deletion in workflows.tsx) therefore leave rows pointing at steps/bookings whose reminders no longer exist. For workflow/step deletion the cascade cleans up, but for the reschedule path the old booking is only cancelled, so stale reminder rows accumulate until their `scheduledDate` passes. Delete the row after the successful cancel request.

findings.title: PrismaPromise imported as a value from @prisma/client
findings.body: `PrismaPromise` (and in part `Prisma`) was changed from `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` to a value import. `PrismaPromise` is a type-only export of @prisma/client; importing it in a value import statement makes the bundler/runtime try to resolve a non-existent runtime binding, which can break the build or throw at module load. Keep it as a type-only import.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation promises are not awaited
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but called without `await` inside `forEach`, and their results are no longer added to `prismaPromises`. The handler can return (and the serverless function can be frozen/terminated) before the `workflowReminder` update/delete or the Twilio cancel completes, so reminders may silently stay active. Collect the promises and await them. The same pattern exists in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (requestReschedule) and `handleNewBooking.ts`, where the surrounding try/catch also cannot catch rejections of un-awaited promises.
